commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Repository history after the base commit is out of bounds. This issue was
solved on master after the base commit; do not read, fetch, log, diff or
check out anything newer than the base commit named above, do not look at
closed pull requests or issue comments, and do not search master for the
landed solution. Solve it from the base commit and the issue text below.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer

I'll begin by checking the checkout is clean and moving to the pinned base commit, then read the matrix doc and the reference JS/TS rows.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
I'm checking whether the C resolver can bind a free function like `connect` declared in an external header. That decides whether this row can land or has to stop as a capability gap.
Start the test-binary build in the background while I write the fixture.

Meanwhile, write the C finding fixture and probe policy.
Still compiling the analysis crate; the probe test is ready and runs when it finishes.
I'm querying `procedure-effects` and call-relation rows through the CLI on the C fixture to see exactly which callee stays unresolved.
Running two probes: a pure C chain (does keying work?) and a resolved `-isystem` header root (does `connect` bind?). One is slow, so I'm polling its output.
The pure-C chain returned no diagnostics, so keying works and the run completes. The `-isystem` probe is still running.
The clippy run is going in the background. Meanwhile I'm cleaning the test policy `c.rqlp`, which still carries Rust wording in its header.
My replacement mangled a comment; fixing it.
Formatting is clean. Now clippy in the background, with a full test-suite run of the file afterwards.
Clippy is clean. Now the whole 3387 test file, then commit.

FINAL REPORT

The C row is blocked by a resolver gap, so I did not ship the row. The base is `18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19`. I committed the fixtures, the gap-pinning tests and the matrix note, and left #3457 open. I did not run `analysis --lib` or the C++ usage/issue suites, because no graph or usages code changed.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The external identity the effect relation keys on is `<owner>.<member>`. C has no `::` and no class or namespace, so a bare `connect(...)` has no owner to publish.
The only fallback that would make it bind is matching the spelling `connect`, which is the same-name near miss this family exists to reject.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## 1. Confirmed cause
The fixture chain is `price_total -> audit_record -> audit_send -> connect`, with `#include <sys/socket.h>` in `audit_client.c`.
- **Callee stays name-only:** `candidates_of` on the `connect` token reports `{candidate_kind: external_route, name: "connect"}`. The tier is `external_root`, the boundary is `external_unknown`, and the outcome is `rejected` (`boundary_blocked`).
- **Effect set stays open:** `procedure-effects` on `audit_send` reports coverage `open`, derivation `incomplete` and reason `dispatch_unresolved`. The policy run is `Inconclusive`, with `absence-requires-exhaustive-coverage` and `EffectDerivationIncomplete`.
- **An include root does not help:** with a `compile_commands.json` giving `-isystem` to a directory holding `sys/socket.h`, the boundary becomes `external_declared_unindexed`. The candidate is still name-only and the effect set is still open.
- **Why no identity is minted (from the code):** `canonical_external_callee` in `usages/call_relations.rs` returns `None` unless `split_canonical_qualified_callee` yields an owner.
  - The C++ external header route in `cpp/external.rs` answers type members and namespaces, not free functions.
  - The only free-function route is the `has_unresolved_include_visible_before` arm in `get_definition/cpp.rs` (#3466). It publishes a name-only boundary from the include fact.
- **Keying is not the problem:** the corrected tree, whose whole reachable graph is analyzed workspace code, concludes with zero findings and a `Complete` run.

  - `the_c_corrected_tree_keys_its_workspace_callees_and_concludes_clean` passes.
  - `a_c_system_header_free_function_call_binds_no_reviewed_identity_yet` passes and pins the gap.
  - `a_c_system_header_free_function_call_binds_the_reviewed_posix_identity` is `#[ignore]` and expects one finding, so it fails with zero findings until the gap closes.
- **Matrix note:** the C row and a new section carry the evidence.
- **Not delivered:** the recursion, near-miss and unresolved fixtures, the CLI exit-code run and the MCP run. Every one of them depends on the binding that does not exist yet.
- **No extraction epoch bump:** no persisted fact changed.

## 5. State, limitations, separately actionable
`git status --short` is clean.

I could not file the capability-gap issue: I was told not to touch GitHub, and no issue-creation permission was given. The draft is below.

> **Draft issue: C/C++ resolver needs a header-scoped external free-function identity.** A bare free function declared in a system or library header (`connect` from `<sys/socket.h>`, `curl_easy_perform`) has no owner segment. The resolver reports a name-only `external_route` boundary, `canonical_external_callee` mints no identity, and reviewed summaries cannot bind. Wanted: bind a free-function identity scoped to the declaring header, resolved through the include closure the file reaches, and publish it through `canonical_external_callee`. Blocks #3457 and #3458.

## 6. Draft approach comment for #3457
I could not land the C row, because the C resolver cannot bind an exact identity for `connect` from `<sys/socket.h>`. On the finding fixture, the call reports only a name-only `external_route` candidate with boundary `external_unknown`, and `procedure-effects` on the helper reports coverage `open`, reason `dispatch_unresolved`. An explicit `-isystem` root moves the boundary to `external_declared_unindexed` but still mints no identity. The cause is that the external identity is `<owner>.<member>`, and C has no owner segment for a bare free function. The C++ header route only answers type members and namespaces. Keying is fine: the corrected tree concludes clean with a `Complete` run. I did not add a shipped model or specialization, since matching the spelling `connect` is the near miss this family rejects. I committed the fixtures, a passing test that pins the gap and an ignored test that expects the finding once it closes. The fix is a resolver change: a header-scoped free-function identity from the include closure. It also serves C++ (#3458), so I suggest a separate capability issue.
